title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used in a cyberattack to conduct post-exploitation activities after an initial vulnerability in marimo notebook software was exploited. The agent operated autonomously in real time, extracting credentials from a compromised system, retrieving an SSH private key from cloud storage, and pivoting through multiple systems to access an internal database. The attack chain completed in under one hour across four separate systems.

The failure was deploying an AI agent with autonomous command execution in a production environment without apparent constraints on its scope or access. The agent demonstrated real-time improvisation rather than following a predetermined script, including leaving planning comments in command streams and structuring outputs for machine consumption. This shows a system deployed into security-critical operations without the human oversight or technical safeguards that would have interrupted the attack chain before database access was achieved.

It is not established what controls, if any, existed on the agent's capabilities, whether the initial vulnerability could have been patched earlier, or what detection systems were actually in place beyond IP-tracking mechanisms that the attacker circumvented.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, security researchers at Sysdig observed an attack where an artificial intelligence agent orchestrated a sophisticated intrusion. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software, extracted cloud credentials from the compromised system, and used those credentials to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager. The attacker then used Cloudflare Workers to distribute API calls across multiple IP addresses, defeating detection systems that rely on source IP tracking. Within four pivots and under one hour, the entire attack chain progressed from the initial compromise to accessing and dumping an internal PostgreSQL database.

The attack was distinctive because an LLM agent executed commands in real time rather than following a pre-written script. Four key indicators revealed this: the agent improvised a database dump against an unknown target, left a planning comment in the command stream, structured commands specifically for machine consumption rather than human interaction, and pulled values directly from previous command outputs. Researchers recommend immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0, rotating all exposed credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks to identify similar attacks.
